bullets.title: Market structurally risk-on: S&P flat ~7,758, VIX ticking up to 15.13 with options skewing bullish
bullets.body: S&P 500 essentially flat at 7,758 while VIX nudged +1.5% to 15.13. Options sentiment remains decisively risk-on with calls at 58% of contracts; Goldman Panic Index at lowest since before 2024. Leveraged ETF SPX exposure is highest in over a year and systematic CTA sell triggers have been pushed further away. Goldman warns equities struggle if 10Y yields exceed ~5% nominal or ~2.75% real.

bullets.title: 2Q earnings season broadly strong: 87% S&P beat rate, median Russell 2000 EPS +15%
bullets.body: 87% of S&P 500 companies beat EPS in 2Q26 (up from 82% prior quarter), with S&P tracking ~30% YoY EPS growth. Russell 3000 median EPS growth at 15% (strongest since 2021) and revenue growth at 8% (highest since 2023). 76% of industry groups show positive EPS revisions breadth near cycle high; market is rewarding quality, FCF, and AI adopters over semis. Stocks with upward EPS AND FCF revisions outperformed by 1.6% post-reporting.

bullets.title: MS CIO Wilson: early-to-mid cycle rotation — overweight Financials, Hyperscalers over Semis, Discretionary Goods
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley CIO Wilson sees leadership shifting from lower to higher quality as the market transitions from early to mid-cycle. He prefers Hyperscalers over Semis given strong core businesses and underappreciated AI ROI, and sees Consumer Discretionary Goods as compelling as wallet shifts from services to goods. Principal risks remain acceleration in back-end yields and/or crude.

bullets.title: CPI Wednesday: JPM forecasts headline +3.6% YoY, core +2.4%; hawkish print (-1.5%-2.5%) more painful than dovish upside
bullets.body: JPM forecasts August headline CPI at 3.6% YoY (up from 3.4% in July) and core CPI steady at 2.4% YoY; core PCE at 3.3% YoY. A core MoM above 0.30% (5% probability) implies SPX -1.5% to -2.5%; a 0.20%-0.25% print (40% probability) yields +25-75bps. Apple's June PC/tablet price hikes (+15%/+20%) may add ~1.5% to education/communication goods CPI. Bond market more sensitive to hawkish surprises than equities.

bullets.title: Sticky inflation despite soft data: core PCE +3.8% annualized over 6 months, consumer expectations rising
bullets.body: Core PCE deflator has run at 3.8% annualized over the past 6 months, well above the Fed's 2% target. Consumer inflation expectations ticked to 3.5% YoY in July. Excess liquidity (M2 accelerating, rates below nominal GDP growth, easing bank lending standards) keeps inflation sticky. GDP price deflator running +4.3% YoY with acceleration in tech and government components diverging from core PCE.

bullets.title: Term premium structurally higher: rising federal debt + stock-bond correlation shift from 'ice' to 'fire' regime
bullets.body: Two structural forces are pushing term premium higher post-Covid: a steepening federal debt/GDP path and a shift in stock-bond correlation from negative ('ice') to positive ('fire'). Both forces are durable — escape from the liquidity trap is sustained by upward pressure on r*, and the inflation regime shift is unlikely to reverse quickly. The research notes the 'easy part' of the steepening call is behind us as negative 100bps+ term premium was the anomaly, not positive 100bps.

bullets.title: US labor market stronger than headline payrolls suggest; 7 timelier indicators all accelerating
bullets.body: Seven leading labor indicators — claims, NFIB hiring (up 9pts to 2022 highs), real revenues, CEO confidence, EDI, ISM/PMI, and FAST sales — all show solid employment momentum, contradicting soft headline payrolls. Prime-age labor force participation (25-54) is near all-time highs, driven by goods-producing jobs with a 6x job multiplier. Foreign growth, however, is likely peaking with PMIs rolling over and US-bound exports decelerating.

bullets.title: AI capex estimates surging toward ~$900B this year and $1.2T+ next year; SpaceX 8-10GW by 2027 seen feasible
bullets.body: AI capex estimates are being revised toward ~$900B for 2026 and $1.2T+ for 2027. SemiAnalysis argues SpaceX targeting 8-10GW by end of 2027 is feasible, with frontier inference potentially generating >$100B/GW/year revenue. Anthropic alone has signed $19B compute deal with TeraWulf, is in talks for $10B with Meta and $15B loan for a 1.6GW Texas data center, and signed multi-billion AMD chip deal. WFE market run-rating ~$170-175B in CQ4 with $200B+ expected next year.

bullets.title: IT Hardware upgraded to In-Line at MS: 'Fear of Missing Procurement' pulling forward Server/Storage spend into 2027-28
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgrades the IT Hardware sector from Cautious to In-Line, upgrading HPE and P to Overweight, citing chipflation-driven 'Fear of Missing Procurement' accelerating enterprise spending rather than delaying it. AlphaWise survey shows 70-75% of CIOs pulling forward 2026 PC/Storage/Server spending; 60% planning on-prem AI capacity expansion. The server/storage upcycle is expected to extend to 2027-2028, with PC rollover expected in 2H26/2027.

bullets.title: MSFT-SpaceX compute deal could be 3GW; Maia 300 custom chip targets 300K+ units in 2027
bullets.body: Microsoft is potentially becoming SpaceX's largest compute offtaker at ~3GW, which could accelerate Azure growth from 42% to >100% next year per Morgan Stanley. MSFT is also escalating its custom AI silicon with the Maia 300 chip targeting a September 2026 unveiling, scaling to 300K+ chips in 2027 versus tens of thousands of Maia 200s. Both developments reduce external supplier dependence and strengthen Azure's competitive position.

bullets.title: Memory cycle: DRAM undersupply extends to 2028; MU and SK Hynix poised for 80%+ GMs; HBM tight through 2027
bullets.body: JPM raises its FY26-28 global memory TAM by 4-8% to $971B/$1.44T/$1.83T with DRAM supply-demand shortage persisting through 2027. Micron's own conference commentary signals DRAM imbalance tighter in 2027 than 2026, with $250B investment plan and $22B+ in upfront customer commitments. HBM bit shipments forecast to grow 50-60% YoY in 2027 but insufficient to meet demand, sustaining pricing power through 2027. MU and SK Hynix are expected to generate unprecedented FCF with 16-20% cash yields over three years.

bullets.title: INTC $15B equity raise dilutes CY27 EPS 3.3% but is seen as positive for WFE suppliers; demand oversubscribed
bullets.body: Intel announced a ~$15B common stock offering (plus ~$2.25B greenshoe) to fund next-generation leading-edge capex in Arizona, Ireland, and Ohio fabs. Aggregate demand exceeded the offering size. The raise dilutes CY27 EPS by ~$0.06 or 3.3%, but is seen as rational at current price. The key read-through is bullish for WFE suppliers (ASML, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC).

bullets.title: PC notebook ODM shipments collapse 27% m/m in July; KeyBanc cuts 3Q forecast to -4% q/q — bearish for AMD, INTC, MU
bullets.body: July PC notebook ODM units came in at 12.2M versus a 13.3M estimate, down 27% m/m and 19% y/y, with Quanta missing on weak Apple demand and Compal on weak Dell demand. KeyBanc now forecasts 3Q at 41.9M units (-4% q/q, -12% y/y) and full-year 2026 at -8% to -12% y/y. 4Q is expected -15% q/q / -20% y/y, with memory price increases seen as a primary demand headwind following 1H pull-ins.

bullets.title: Optical stocks rallying sharply on memory rotation; elevated setup risk as LITE/COHR report this week
bullets.body: Optical names (LITE, COHR, AAOI) surged +43-44% in one week on rotation out of memory stocks. Memory sentiment flipped rapidly — MU down 15% since July 1, SNDK down 40% vs semis -6% — despite limited fundamental change. Mizuho flags elevated setup risk into LITE and COHR reports due Tuesday/Wednesday given the sharp moves; Hedgeye came away more negative on the memory cycle post-FMS conference as hyperscalers push back on pricing/terms.

bullets.title: 52-week high breadth positive: 86 names above $5B hit highs, led by PANW +126%, NTAP +93%, SNOW +64%
bullets.body: 86 S&P-listed stocks (market cap >$5B) hit 52-week highs on August 10 versus only 22 new lows. Notable large-cap highs include PANW (+126% on the year), NTAP (+93%), SNOW (+64%), and ABNB (+51%). Health Technology led with 23 highs; Technology Services had 12 highs.

bullets.title: Pre-market tape: HPE +5% on MS upgrade, META +1.7% on AI announcements; INTC -4.6%, AAPL -1.2% on downgrades
bullets.body: In pre-market trading, HPE gained 5% on the Morgan Stanley upgrade to Overweight, META rose 1.7% on Zuckerberg's open-model announcements including Muse Glimmer. On the downside, INTC fell 4.6% on the $15B equity offering, AAPL dropped 1.2% after Jefferies downgraded to Underperform on the all-glass iPhone cancellation, and TTD fell 2.2% after multiple downgrades. MU was down 1.8%, NET -2.1% on its convertible offering, and HUBS -1.4%.

bullets.title: AAPL downgraded to Underperform at Jefferies: all-glass iPhone canceled, ASP CAGR cut from 9% to 6.8%, PT $264
bullets.body: Jefferies downgrades Apple to Underperform with a $264 PT (16% downside) after supply chain checks confirm cancellation of the 20th anniversary all-glass iPhone due to low yield. The all-glass model was a key driver of higher ASPs; its removal cuts FY28/29 EPS by 2.1%/3.4%. Foldable iPhones remain niche at ~14M units, and rising memory costs (iPhone 18 Pro BOM up ~38-40% YoY, memory jumping from 10% to 34% of BOM) further pressure margins.

bullets.title: Cloudflare FedRAMP High authorization expands addressable federal/DoD market; NET issuing $2.175B convertible
bullets.body: Cloudflare achieved FedRAMP High Authorization and announced GovRAMP Moderate authorization, with IL4 authorization also being pursued, meaningfully expanding its addressable federal and DoD market. Separately, NET announced a $2.175B convertible offering, which pressured the stock -2.1% in pre-market. Q2 results showed revenue +36% YoY, re-accelerated for 4 of last 5 quarters, with DBNR +120% and headcount cut ~14% while guiding revenue higher.

bullets.title: GS strategists turn more constructive on China soft-tech ADRs vs hard-tech: trough valuations, narrowing losses
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs strategists are incrementally more constructive on offshore China internet/soft-tech ADRs versus hard-tech peers, citing substantial underperformance, cycle-trough valuations, narrowing subsidy losses, and improving AI monetization. BABA cloud revenue expected to accelerate 7 points to 45% YoY growth in 2Q; SE is -11% YTD but +45% from its March trough. China internet profits forecast to decline -12% YTY in June quarter, a meaningful improvement from -35%/-31% in prior two quarters.

bullets.title: Softlines retail: July prices +3.1% YoY but promos jumped 100bps, inventory weeks up 12% — tariff offsets with selective consumer
bullets.body: UBS Evidence Lab finds softgoods prices rose ~3.1% YoY in July but the Promotional Discount Factor rose ~100bps YoY to ~18.9% and Discount Breadth increased ~160bps — the first YoY increase in Discount Depth in 23 months. Inventory weeks-of-supply are up ~12% YoY. The data suggests brands are passing tariff costs through on price but competing aggressively on promotion, consistent with a selective consumer backdrop.
